text:
elena: Starting canary bring-up for solstice9b-v1 (int4). Seeing intermittent OOMs under bursty traffic + memory fragmentation spikes on node pool 3. Latency ~2x baseline on 512-token sequences. Anyone seen this pattern before?

raj: saw something similar on a diff model — fragmentation + slowgen when max_new_tokens is large and prefetch is on. can you paste the runtime config and OOM trace?

elena: Dumped one OOM stack + runtime telemetry here: https://redwood.internal/trace/solstice9b/4321009876 
elena: OOM log snippet: `AllocationError: CUDA OOM while allocating 1.8GiB for KV cache` then lots of small alloc/free churn in driver.

noah: quick thought: try lowering default max_new_tokens for canary to 128 and enable microbatching=4. For int4 we saw ~30% mem reduction with microbatching on similar arch. Also try disabling KV prefetch.

irene: quality check: I ran a small eval (100 prompts) on int4 w/ microbatch=4 and max_new=128 — avg ROUGE dropped 0.6% for summarization, but generation artifacts concentrated in first 16 tokens. Could be quantization head bias.

raj: plan: first mitigate OOMs -> config tweak. then run focused evals on prefix tokens and consider per-layer scale fine-tune or symmetric per-channel clipping.

elena: current canary config: 
```
model: solstice9b-v1
quant: int4
batching:
  microbatch_size: 4
  max_new_tokens: 128
  windowed_batching: true
prefetch: false
slot_reserve: 0.12
soft_eviction: true
```

elena: applied this to 2/5 canary nodes at 12:37 PST. OOM rate dropped but latency still spiky on long sequences. memory defrag metrics show smaller peaks but more frequent small allocs.

ops-bot: Deployment event: canary update by elena to solstice9b-v1 applied to nodepool-3 (2/5) at 2026-03-22T20:37:12Z.

raj: followup: try enabling a small KV-trim threshold for long sessions so we don't hold stray prefixes. Example: `kv.max_prefix_bytes=64MB` and `kv.trim_policy=last_accessed` — that trimmed tail memory in earlier runs.

noah: ran a quick A/B between microbatch=4/max_new=128 vs microbatch=2/max_new=256. The former wins on OOMs and p95 latency; the latter better on mean latency for short responses. Depending on SLA we should bias to safety.

irene: for the -0.6% ROUGE we saw, I profiled token logits and it's mostly FQ artifacts in layer 1. We could try symmetric per-channel rescale on layernorm inputs before quantizing. Low-risk experiment: apply per-channel weight scale on first 2 layers.

elena: Proposed rollout plan: 1) keep microbatch=4, max_new_tokens=128, prefetch=false for canary until 1% OOM rate threshold or 30m steady. 2) run targeted quant-rescale experiment on a dedicated canary node (A/B) with 5k eval prompts. 3) if quality delta <1% and OOMs stay low, ramp to 50% then full. Otherwise rollback to float16 variant.

raj: add health check: emit `oom_rate`, `mem_frag_score`, `kv_cache_bytes` to console pulse every 30s and alert if oom_rate>0.01. Also add a temporary soft-fallback model route (solstice9b-fp16) for heavy tails.

elena: doing that now. will also add an eval job for the per-layer rescale. scheduling it for tomorrow morning. thanks all. :thumbsup:

noah: FYI I pushed a small CI that automates the microbatch vs max_new sweep — link: https://ci.redwood/inference/sweeps/solstice9b/4321

elena: noted. if we see quality regressions concentrated at prefix, we can also try a 2-token warmup in fp16 then quant switch (hybrid warmstart) as a mitigation.

irene: sounds good. I'll prepare the evaluation slices focusing on first-32 tokens and conversational prompts.

ops-bot: Alert cleared: transient OOM spike on nodepool-3 resolved after canary config change.

elena: closing loop — will post regression numbers + whether we need quant-rescale next. cheers.
